record: EyeCU-Tracking-Val-v1 GT annotation conventions and methodological decisions
status: FROZEN before the remaining three sequences are annotated

box_convention.rule: Tight visible-person extent with a small practical tolerance at this resolution; no deliberate horizontal safety margin; no shadow; do not infer fully hidden body extent; a partially visible person is annotated consistently.
box_convention.not_the_authority: the A@960 detector. GT is not tuned for IoU agreement with the model under evaluation, in either direction.
box_convention.women_1_decision: KEEP the existing annotation. It is altered only where human visual QC identifies clearly excessive background margin -- never automatically, and never from an IoU statistic.

box_audit_observation.status: QA OBSERVATION, not a reason to alter GT
box_audit_observation.measured_against: the frozen detector preannotations, all 300 frames of women_1_239
box_audit_observation.scale_caveat: At these target sizes the 1.39x width ratio is about 4.6 px of total width. A ratio computed on 13-18 px objects magnifies a difference of a few pixels, and must be read with the absolute numbers beside it.
box_audit_observation.apparent_person_width: NOT MEASURED. No reliable estimator exists here for 13-18 px targets over grass, stands and crowd; chroma or GrabCut segmentation fails on the cases that matter and would count shadow as body, which the convention excludes. A number from an unreliable method would be worse than none.

hota_thresholds.correction_of: an earlier statement in this project that treated IoU >= 0.5 as the HOTA operating point
hota_thresholds.aggregation: trackeval/metrics/_base_metric.py _summary_row reduces every float_array_field with 100 * np.mean(results_[h]); the reported HOTA is therefore the mean over all 19 alphas.
hota_thresholds.clear_and_identity: CLEAR (MOTA) and Identity (IDF1) use a single similarity threshold, default 0.5.
hota_thresholds.consequence: The IoU >= 0.5 share is a DIAGNOSTIC of box-convention agreement only. It is not the fraction of detections that fail aggregate HOTA, and must never be reported as such.

occlusion.rule: CVAT occluded is preserved per visible annotation in the canonical EyeCU JSON as a BOOLEAN.
occlusion.forbidden: Inventing a numeric visibility fraction from that boolean. The annotator marked a binary fact; a fraction would look like a measurement while carrying no information anyone supplied.

mot_visibility_justification.finding: The MotChallenge2DBox loader never reads the visibility column. It slices time_data[:, 2:6] for boxes, column 1 for ids, column 6 for the zero-marked/confidence flag and column 7 for class; column 8 is untouched in both _load_raw_file and get_preprocessed_seq_data.
mot_visibility_justification.therefore: Keeping visibility = 1 changes nothing for the HOTA, CLEAR or Identity metrics we intend to run.
mot_visibility_justification.revisit_if: a later, explicitly defined evaluation protocol requires visibility-aware handling; at that point the canonical JSON already holds the annotator's marks.

long_gap_identity_policy.default: A long-gap reconnect is NEVER accepted automatically. Every event is recorded HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED until a person decides.
long_gap_identity_policy.if_confident: Where the same physical person can be confidently established across the disappearance and re-entry, preserve the same identity.
long_gap_identity_policy.if_uncertain: Do not guess. Start a NEW GT identity and record an uncertain-reentry QC event.
long_gap_identity_policy.insufficient_evidence: Role or team-kit similarity alone does not establish physical identity.
long_gap_identity_policy.forbidden_because: The benchmark exists to judge trackers. GT built from tracker output would be marking its own homework.
long_gap_identity_policy.jump_distance_caveat: The recorded jump is image-space displacement between the last and first observation. The camera moves during these gaps, so it is not a measure of how far the person walked.
